objective_text.T63.01.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_write(arena,logical_capacity,offset,input,n) for an original32-byte arena. Reject capacity>31, offset>capacity or n>capacity-offset before any write; write only the admitted span. Byte31 is a sentinel outside the logical object. Compare with the supplied faulty teaching path that validates only the32-byte physical extent; attacker controls offset/n/data and harmless success is sentinel change.

Then Split the logical object into a real heap allocation and run the isolated faulty path under ASan; compare deterministic model evidence with environment-dependent undefined execution and mitigation effects.

sets.title: Allocation arithmetic and truncation

objective_text.T63.02.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_extent(count,stride,limit,out) using uint32_t inputs and uint64_t arithmetic; accept only product<=limit and product<=UINT32_MAX, publish the product on success, otherwise preserve out. sets.title: Temporal identity and stale access

objective_text.T63.03.a: Derive and defend: Prove a stale token cannot authorize current-incarnation access, state the trusted token origin and require retirement before generation wrap. Compare with an actual heap use-after-free sanitizer target without treating allocator reuse as guaranteed.
objective_text.T63.03.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_read(arena,claimed_generation,index,out): require live==1, matching generation and index<16 before publishing a byte. Failed reads leave out unchanged. The original arena remains allocated, so the stale-handle witness is defined C behavior; attacker retains an old token across reuse and attempts to read a new synthetic occupant.
objective_text.T63.03.c: Falsify and transfer: The mutant ignores generation and reveals a new occupant’s synthetic byte through an old token. This demonstrates a confidentiality violation in the target, not a read primitive against another process. Then Add asynchronous completion retaining a token, then release/reuse the slot before completion. Design cancellation and retirement so old callbacks cannot expose the new occupant.

sets.title: Owned arena views and authorization

objective_text.T63.04.a: Derive and defend: Specify representation, operations, ownership and failure semantics of a checked view. Identify exactly what runtime checks enforce and what trusted-caller discipline or external verification must guarantee.
objective_text.T63.04.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_authorize(arena,principal,generation,begin,length): require live1, exact owner and generation, begin<=16 and length<=16-begin; return admission only, without exposing a pointer on failure. principal is supplied by a trusted harness channel, not copied from request bytes. Define the trusted boundary and compare with a forged-request owner field.

sets.title: Bounded control-flow corruption analysis

objective_text.T63.05.a: Derive and defend: State attacker control, target-local effect and limits. Distinguish data-only unauthorized dispatch from demonstrated arbitrary code execution; analyze control-flow integrity separately from operation authorization.
objective_text.T63.05.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_dispatch(op,grant,sentinel) with op0 read-only no-op and op1 set sentinel77, allowed only when trusted grant==1. Reject unknown op and nonboolean grant before mutation. Analyze the supplied intentionally flawed dispatcher that checks only op range; attacker-controlled op1 without grant must change only the synthetic sentinel in the faulty build.

Then Add a table of three trusted callbacks and a corrupted index inside the original program; compare range checks, read-only dispatch tables and compiler CFI while recording only observed target effects.

sets.title: Format-string authority and byte-preserving logging

objective_text.T63.06.a: Derive and defend: Identify which argument is interpreted as a format and prove the repaired path treats attacker bytes as data. Discuss embedded NUL, truncation policy and logging integrity separately.
objective_text.T63.06.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_log_copy(input,n,output,capacity) copying exact bytes and appending NUL, requiring n<capacity and no overlap; failure leaves output unchanged. Percent bytes have no interpretation. Compare an original isolated printf(user_format) target using the fixed synthetic string%n and a supplied local integer pointer with printf("%s",user_text); the harmless witness is only that integer changing.
objective_text.T63.06.c: Falsify and transfer: Blindly replacing percent with a question mark suppresses the witness but corrupts the required logged bytes. The real repair separates interpreter control from untrusted data. Then Add structured binary logging with explicit length and escaping at display time; test embedded NUL and terminal-control bytes without confusing storage fidelity with safe rendering.

sets.title: Exactly-once release and error cleanup

objective_text.T63.07.a: Derive and defend: Prove ownership conservation and exactly-one destructor call under every failure prefix. Explain why nulling one alias cannot revoke another copied raw pointer.
objective_text.T63.07.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_release(MDOwner) requiring owned exactly1, setting owned0 and incrementing releases once. Repeat release returns0 unchanged. Reject a release counter atUINT_MAX before state change. Build an allocation/failure schedule with caller, queue and callback owners and record every transfer.

sets.title: Observable work, timing and mitigation limits

objective_text.T63.08.a: Derive and defend: Separate functional equality, source-level work count, emitted branches and measured timing. State memory-validity, compiler and CPU assumptions and residual cache/power/speculation channels.
objective_text.T63.08.b: Implement and investigate: Implement md_equal(a,b,n,steps) scanning all n bytes, accumulating XOR difference, reporting steps=n and returning equality. Empty spans compare equal without dereference. Compare with an intentionally early-exit mutant using synthetic secrets only. Inspect optimized code and measure distributions without treating equal loop counts as a universal constant-time guarantee.
objective_text.T63.08.c: Falsify and transfer: The early-exit mutant reports only one step for a first-byte mismatch, leaking a prefix relation. ASan can remain clean because the defect is confidentiality, not invalid memory access. Then Change optimization, vectorization and unequal-length policy; derive what remains observable and compare hardened library behavior only as an external benchmark, not a replacement for the first-principles implementation.
